Graph of the Curves of a Random Smooth

Source: R/plot_random.R
plot_curves.Rd

Selects the graph of a random smooth, random(~ s(x) | g): one thin curve for each level of the grouping factor, over the range of the variable within that level. The graph reads the covariates and requires data.

Usage

plot_curves(n_grid = 100, population = FALSE)

Arguments

n_grid

The number of points of each curve.

population

Whether to add the population smooth of the variable.

Value

A PlotCurves object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The curve of a level is its contribution to the predictor of the equation, \(g_j(x) = a_{0j} + N(x) a_j + Z(x) \delta_j\), the departure of the level from the curve that the other terms of the equation describe. It is centred around zero and does not include the population curve. With population = TRUE the population curve, taken from the single smooth of the same variable in the same equation, is added to each curve and drawn as a thick line, so that the curves are the curves of the levels.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_caterpillar()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(240), id = factor(rep(1:8, each = 30)))
dd$y <- sin(2 * pi * dd$x) + rnorm(8, sd = 0.4)[dd$id] * dd$x +
  rnorm(240, sd = 0.3)
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x) + random(~ s(x) | id),
               distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "random(~s(x)|id)", type = plot_curves(),
                  data = dd)
